newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee runs out of steam, ends below $1,700.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee runs out of steam, ends below $1,700.

text.p: Robusta futures ran out of breath in their attempt to catch up with galloping New York Arabica prices, and skidded below $1,700 a tonne at Thursday's close.

"There has been some liquidation by disappointed longs who bought this morning," said one trader. "You've mainly got short-term guys out here who are looking for $10-$15 profit. That's why the market is so choppy," he added.
Fuelled by Arabicas, benchmark May Robusta futures spiked higher to $1,718 at the opening but finally lost the foothold above $1,700 in late selling.
It touched a low of $1,636 but ended at $1,660, down $7 on the day, widening the arbitrage against New York to 90 cents. The gap swelled to $1 on the March at the close.
Traders said nerves were stretched to the limit by the sharp price gyrations with London being caught up between the rocketing New York and the availability of more Robustas as a result of the rally.
CSCE March Arabica futures soared to a new contract high of 180.50 cents after a round of new speculative buying broke the market through key resistance.
The March/May spread, a barometer of nearby supplies, surged to 12 cents.
London players meanwhile were on guard for a speculative liquidation on nearbys, especially before the President's Day in the United States on Monday.
"London is trying to pre-empt a drop in New York before the long weekend," said one trader.
Thursday's turnover reached a hefty 10,467 lots in the second consecutive active day.
Colombian union leaders were meeting with government ministers on Thursday in an effort to end a strike by 800,000 state sector workers which also affected the transportation of coffee to ports.
But with the government battling to rein in a burgeoning budget deficit, there were doubts whether there could be a quick deal. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8072
